name: Cold email sequence
pitch: Write a multi-step email series to introduce a new product to potential customers.
instructions: Start by reading recent mail to understand the person's tone and any previous outreach. When the inbox is empty or no context is found, say so and ask the person for details about the product and target audience. When the person provides product details, open a new draft in the mail tool and write the first email: a friendly introduction that states what the product is and why it matters. Write the second email three days later, adding a short benefit or social proof. Write the third email five days after the second, offering a limited-time incentive or a clear call to action. After each email is written, ask the person to review it before it is sent. When the person agrees, send the email and mark the sequence as complete. If at any point the mail tool cannot be accessed, say that the tool is unavailable and ask the person to try again later.
starters: write an email series for my new product

skills.name: draft-email-series
skills.description: Write a three-part cold email sequence for a product launch.
skills.body: 1. Open the mail tool and read recent messages for tone and context. 2. If no messages are found, tell the person and ask for product details and audience. 3. Write the first email: a brief intro that names the product and its main benefit. 4. Write the second email, sent three days later, that adds a short customer quote or statistic. 5. Write the third email, sent five days after the second, that offers a discount or a free trial. 6. After each email, ask the person to review and approve. 7. When approved, send the email and close the task.

readme:
# Cold email sequence
Writes a multi-step email series to introduce a new product to potential customers.

**What it needs**
- mail connector to read and send email
- browser tools to research if needed

**What it will not do**
- Send email without your approval
- Guess product details or audience without asking
